executiveSummary: GM0269's official 2025 identity, contained reference point, 24,417-resident control, 26 neighbourhood records, six BAG places, fifteen BRT settlements and five logical road-border links are coherent, and all ten canonical presets execute deterministically at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across eight services. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Oldebroek spans Drontermeer/Randmeren-side polders, regulated surface-water and seepage systems, the Veluwe flank, villages and extensive heath/forest including the Artillerie Schietkamp. Official municipal evidence distinguishes primary Randmeerdijken, the Gelderse Gracht/De Wenden drainage chain, Drontermeer inlet, polder bottlenecks and urban groundwater/rain nuisance; these are not represented by one generic water scalar. The major-river preset may have an indirect IJssel–Reevediep–Drontermeer/Randmeren pathway, but its exact persistent 2.712616 m depth, 498 to 579 affected residents and 241,915 to 955,130 person-hours at T+24 to T+72 lack a selected boundary level, defence state, breach/overtopping footprint or control operation. Conversely, direct North Sea coastal depth zero does not establish Randmeren or polder safety. Wildfire is the clearest contradiction: VNOG records 3,005 ha of nature, real ASK/heath/forest fires and a scenario affecting camps, roads, villages and insufficiently self-reliant visitors, yet a controlled ignition inside Verspreide huizen Oldebroekse Heide reports flame 0.628598, smoke 0.592788 and zero affected people while ranking the source neighbourhood sixth behind Hattemerbroek and polder areas. Eight active single hazards share one exact 26-neighbourhood order. Two official rows also share the label Verspreide huizen Oosterwolde and must remain disambiguated by BU code. The A28 links are one series corridor; source NWB sections labelled route 050 are signed A50/RW50/VBD and must not be presented as an independent anonymous route. Knooppunt Hattemerbroek connects A28, A50 and N50, while N308, N763, Wezep station, rural roads and external Isala Zwolle care create common-mode access dependencies. Public context supplies 97 partial water assets, one large-user electricity-planning sample, provider polygons, 67 antenna sites and 17 schools but no contained Waterinfo, fixed KNMI, RIVM air/care, NDW or warning points. These records do not supply live topology, occupancy, capacity, backup, staffing, outage or restoration. Exact first-72-hour hazard, service and recovery values must remain visibly synthetic or Unknown until incident forcing, dynamic recreation/military/transit population, physical dependencies and confirmed actions/resources are bound; NoData is never zero, open, safe or recovered.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0269 official 2025 identity, neighbourhood, place and settlement inputs
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated municipality and regional snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026; safety-region snapshot retrieved 2 September 2026; public open-data terms apply per PDOK/CBS dataset metadata
supports: Annual CBS/PDOK inputs identify GM0269 as Oldebroek in Gelderland and Veiligheidsregio Noord- en Oost-Gelderland, with 24,417 residents, density 250/km², 21% aged 65 or older and 2,555 one-person households. The reference point [5.939014105637479,52.43661250077501] lies inside the generalized 2025 boundary.

Twenty-six neighbourhoods in three districts sum to 24,415 residents, two below the municipal control (-0.008%); households total 9,645 and rounded age-65-plus rows total 5,135. Deterministic allocation adds two without rewriting observed rows.

The six BAG places are 't Loo Oldebroek, Hattemerbroek, Noordeinde Gld, Oldebroek, Oosterwolde Gld and Wezep; fifteen BRT settlements comprise seven buurtschappen, one deelkern, one gehucht and six woonkernen. No BAG place centre falls outside the generalized boundary.
BU02690208 and BU02690210 are distinct official neighbourhoods but both carry the label Verspreide huizen Oosterwolde; identity and UI joins must use codes rather than labels.

Average home value, housing tenure/type fields each have four null neighbourhood rows, cars per household six, social/AOW/disability fields one each, and district heat/public charging all 26. Null is NoData, not numeric zero or absence.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Omgevingsvisie: water, klimaat en Randmeerdijken
evidenceSources.edition: Municipal environmental vision established 13 December 2018; official strategic/planning context, not a live hydraulic state; reuse licence not stated on inspected page
supports: The municipality extends to Drontermeer and the Randmeren coastal zone; the North Randmeer dikes along Veluwemeer/Drontermeer are primary flood defences.

Polders contain extensive surface water fed partly by Veluwe seepage, while Oldebroek village can experience groundwater nuisance. A 2012 NBW assessment identified bottlenecks in polders Oosterwolde and Oldebroek and more extensive inundation in Oosterwolde.
Municipal policy separates rainwater locally, retains/infiltrates it and distinguishes drought, urban water nuisance, groundwater and surface-water management.

Oldebroek is connected to Delta Programme river work through the lower IJssel/Reevediep and to IJsselmeer-region work through Drontermeer; this supports possible connected pathways, not a universal direct river-depth scalar.

evidenceSources.publisher: Waterschap Vallei en Veluwe and Gemeente Oldebroek
evidenceSources.title: E03 — Hattem–Oosterwolde–Oldebroek water-level decision and current water situation
evidenceSources.edition: Draft level-decision notice dated 17 June 2026, intended adoption in the second half of 2026; waterbeeld separately updated 2 September 2026 13:58 local time; official planning/status context, reuse licence not stated
supports: The draft peilbesluit sets flexible wet/dry target ranges for the Hattem, Oosterwolde and Oldebroek management area, mostly retaining existing ranges and changing part of eastern Oldebroek. A draft normal regime is not proof of event-time level or pump/weir operation.

The water board's 2 September 2026 waterbeeld reported management-area crisis phase 2, groundwater far below seasonal normal, vulnerable recovery, abstraction restrictions and an approximate 250 mm regional precipitation deficit; local conditions vary.

Historical municipal landscape planning documents De Wenden pumping from Oosterwolde/Gelderse Gracht toward Drontermeer, reverse summer inlet and controlled polder drainage. That planning record is contextual, not a current complete asset/connectivity state.
Regional timestamped drought and draft target levels must not be converted into exact GM0269 flood, drinking-water or service percentages without local observations and a selected incident.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2025–2028, bijlagenboek natuurbrand
evidenceSources.edition: Regional risk-profile period 2025–2028; official scenario/planning evidence, not an incident perimeter, forecast or live resource state; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: VNOG records 3,005 ha of nature in Oldebroek and cites Artillerie Schietkamp heath fires in 2003 and 2018 and an Oldebroek forest fire in June 2023.
Its reference scenario uses a 1.5–2.5 km² fire and 5.5–6.5 km² smoke area affecting camps/nature visitors, motorway and village, with inaccessible dry terrain and inadequate extinguishing water.

Camping and nature visitors may be insufficiently self-reliant; mutual-aid resources can become scarce and military support may be relevant. The scenario distinguishes first hour, first four hours and first day actions.
The official scenario demonstrates mechanisms and decision needs but is not a selected Oldebroek ignition, current occupancy, road closure, evacuation order, available crew/water or forecast.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Artillerie Schietkamp 't Harde public exercise context
evidenceSources.edition: Current public page inspected 3 September 2026; week-36 schedule (31 August–4 September 2026) subject to change; official planned activity, not confirmed occupancy or incident forcing; Crown copyright/public reuse subject to rijksoverheid.nl terms
supports: The ASK is the Netherlands' artillery and mortar firing area and spans the northern Oldebroekse Heide and southern Doornspijkse area; the public page describes an approximately 13.5 by 4 km site.
At audit time the public schedule listed daytime exercises Monday through Thursday and Friday morning on the northern/Oldebroekse-Heide side, explicitly subject to change.

Planned activity establishes a transient operational cohort and ignition/access context but not exact personnel, sensitive topology, live occupancy, firing, exclusion zones, resources or causation for a simulator event.
No sensitive military layout, staffing or response capability should be inferred from the public page.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — Drontermeer, A28/A50/N50, N308/N763 and Wezep rail context
evidenceSources.edition: Current RWS/Province infrastructure pages and generated NWB/ProRail/GTFS snapshots inspected 3 September 2026; static/network context, not live passability or capacity; source-specific public-data terms apply
supports: RWS describes Drontermeer as a shallow Randmeer between Kampen and Elburg, about 10 km long and 0.2–1 km wide with bottom depth around -3.00 m NAP. It is not direct North Sea coast, although it can participate in connected lake/river hydraulics.

Five logical border links represent A28 toward Hattem and Elburg, route 050 toward Hattem, N308 toward Elburg and N763 toward Kampen. The two A28 links are series directions of one physical corridor and are non-additive.

The route-050 source sections are signed A50/RW50/VBD in NWB provenance; Knooppunt Hattemerbroek connects A28, A50 and N50. The map must not imply an unidentified independent corridor or add series capacities.

Wezep station and 27 transit stop areas, including Landal Landgoed 't Loo and W. de Zwijgerkazerne, are static/schedule context, not trains, buses, people present, incident access or evacuation throughput.

evidenceSources.publisher: Gemeente Oldebroek, Veiligheidsregio Noord- en Oost-Gelderland and RIVM
evidenceSources.title: E07 — 72-hour preparedness, crisis responsibilities and external acute care
evidenceSources.edition: Current municipal preparedness page and VNOG Crisisplan 2025–2028 inspected 3 September 2026; RIVM acute-care v1.1 deployment snapshot retrieved 2 September 2026; doctrine/facility context, not incident resource commitment
supports: The municipality explicitly prioritises 72-hour self-reliance and identifies holiday parks, care homes, motorway emergency access and trains with passengers as planning concerns.

Municipal work on core-level maps of water points and generators and exercises is described as ongoing. A plan or intended map is not proof that a site, generator, fuel, staff or distribution operation is currently available.

VNOG crisis doctrine defines alerting, command, public care, mobility, medical operations and recovery responsibilities, but not event-specific shelters, transport, crews, stock, completion or restoration.

RIVM v1.1 locates 24/7 Isala Zwolle outside GM0269 about 15.1 km straight-line from the municipal reference point, with acute obstetrics and 20 rooms; routing, ambulance, staffing, generator/fuel, diversion and acceptance remain Unknown.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis, Netbeheer Nederland, Stichting Mijn Aansluiting, RDI, DUO, KNMI, RIVM, Rijkswaterstaat and NDW
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Partial water, utility, telecom, education, care, weather and traffic context
evidenceSources.edition: HWH snapshot retrieved 3 September 2026, CC BY-SA 4.0 with contributor-dependent completeness; other public-context snapshots retrieved 2–3 September 2026 with source-specific editions/licences
supports: Full-resolution containment assigns 97 HWH objects: two sewer pumps with non-null capacity numbers, six sluices, four surface-water pumps and 85 weirs whose capacity fields are null. De Wenden/Oosterwolde–Gelderse Gracht and Noordermerkkanaal names support a managed chain but do not disclose live connectivity or operation.

One 8095PA sample maps to Liander OS Nunspeet 10-2i and reports 29/32 MW existing/required withdrawal and a 14.6 MW/26-request queue; injection is 29/25 MW with 26/20 requests and 28 projects, earliest 2029. This is large-user planning, not current load, outage or reserve.

At the municipal reference point public polygons return Liander electricity/gas, Vitens drinking water, Ziggo media and no drainage match. Provider responsibility is not physical connectivity, pressure, quality, coverage, outage or restoration.
RDI assigns 67 sites and DUO 17 education locations. Registers do not establish coverage/backhaul/power, occupancy, shelter role, staff or supplies.

Zero contained Waterinfo observations/forecasts, fixed KNMI observations/warnings, RIVM PM2.5/acute-care, government-service, NDW-situation and seismic points are scoped NoData, never normal conditions, open routes, available service or safety.
